title: The finite linear dual is a Hopf module
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. A commutative Hopf $k$-algebra here means a unital commutative $k$-algebra $A$ with $k$-algebra maps $\Delta_A:A\to A\otimes_k A$, $\epsilon_A:A\to k$, $S_A:A\to A$ such that $(\Delta_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=(1\otimes\Delta_A)\Delta_A$, $(\epsilon_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=(1\otimes\epsilon_A)\Delta_A=1_A$, and $\mu_A(S_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=\mu_A(1\otimes S_A)\Delta_A=\eta_A\epsilon_A$, under the usual tensor unit and associativity identifications; $\mu_A$ and $\eta_A$ are multiplication and unit. Tensor products are those of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Let $H$ be such a commutative Hopf $k$-algebra with a finite $k$-basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Put $H^*=\operatorname{Hom}_k(H,k)$, with pointwise vector operations, and use module tensors [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Set
$$(h\cdot f)(x)=f(S_H(h)x)\qquad(h,x\in H,\ f\in H^*).$$
There is a unique $k$-linear map $\rho:H^*\to H\otimes_k H^*$ characterized by
$$(1_H\otimes\operatorname{ev}_x)\rho(f)=\sum f(x_{(1)})x_{(2)}\qquad(x\in H),$$
where $\Delta_H(x)=\sum x_{(1)}\otimes x_{(2)}$ and $\operatorname{ev}_x(g)=g(x)$. These formulas give a $k$-bilinear unital associative left $H$-action and a left coaction satisfying
$$(\Delta_H\otimes1)\rho=(1\otimes\rho)\rho,\qquad(\epsilon_H\otimes1)\rho=1_{H^*},$$
$$\rho(h\cdot f)=\sum h_{(1)}f_{(-1)}\otimes(h_{(2)}\cdot f_{(0)}),\qquad\rho(f)=\sum f_{(-1)}\otimes f_{(0)}.$$

source.place: Zheng, Proposition 4.12(2), printed p.8, displayed action and coaction, with diagonal compatibility made explicit; independently Farnsteiner, Hopf Modules and Integrals: The Space of Integrals (26 April 2006), printed p.1. Read online at https://math.uchicago.edu/~may/REU2020/REUPapers/Zheng,Siqi.pdf and https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/~sek/select/HopfMod2.pdf; local documents WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this dual-Hopf-module construction.

proof.text:
The action is well defined because $x\mapsto S_H(h)x$ is $k$-linear; the formula is linear in each of $h,f$. Since $S_H$ is a unital algebra map in the hypotheses, $1\cdot f=f$ and
$$(h\cdot(h'\cdot f))(x)=f(S_H(h')S_H(h)x)=f(S_H(hh')x)=((hh')\cdot f)(x).$$
The middle equality uses commutativity of $H$. Thus these formulas give the asserted bilinear unital associative left action.

proof.text:
Fix the finite basis $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ provided by the hypothesis and write $e_i^*(x)$ for its coordinate functions. Unique coordinates give linearity of $e_i^*$ and $g=\sum_i g(e_i)e_i^*$ for every $g\in H^*$. For any $k$-vector space $V$, tensor bilinearity therefore gives
$$z=\sum_i(1_V\otimes\operatorname{ev}_{e_i})(z)\otimes e_i^*\qquad(z\in V\otimes_kH^*),$$
where the formula is first checked on $v\otimes g$, which generate the tensor product. In particular, all evaluations on the final factor jointly detect equality. Define the linear map $T_f:H\to H$ by $T_f(x)=\sum f(x_{(1)})x_{(2)}$, using the linear tensor contraction of $\Delta_H$; it is also linear in $f$. Set
$$\rho(f)=\sum_i T_f(e_i)\otimes e_i^*.$$
Evaluation at $x$ gives $\sum_i e_i^*(x)T_f(e_i)=T_f(x)$. This constructs the required linear map. The displayed reconstruction with $V=H$ proves uniqueness, so it is independent of the basis.

proof.text:
Evaluate the proposed counit identity at $x\in H$. Step 2 and the tensor universal property give
$$((\epsilon_H\otimes1)\rho(f))(x)=\epsilon_H(T_f(x))=\sum f(x_{(1)})\epsilon_H(x_{(2)})=f(x).$$
The last equality is the counit axiom of $H$, followed by $f$. Equality of linear functionals gives $(\epsilon_H\otimes1)\rho=1_{H^*}$.

proof.text:
Use the tensor associativity identification and evaluate the final $H^*$ factor at $x$. By step 2, the evaluation of $(\Delta_H\otimes1)\rho(f)$ is
$$\Delta_H(T_f(x))=\sum f(x_{(1)})x_{(2)}\otimes x_{(3)}.$$
Writing $\rho(f)=\sum f_{(-1)}\otimes f_{(0)}$, the evaluation of $(1\otimes\rho)\rho(f)$ is
$$\sum f_{(-1)}\otimes f_{(0)}(x_{(1)})x_{(2)}=\sum T_f(x_{(1)})\otimes x_{(2)}=\sum f(x_{(1)})x_{(2)}\otimes x_{(3)}.$$
These expressions agree by coassociativity of $\Delta_H$. The reconstruction in step 2 with $V=H\otimes_kH$ shows equality of the original tensors, proving the coaction law.

proof.text:
Derive the antipode identity needed for compatibility using the cited associative unital convolution algebra $\operatorname{Hom}_k(H,H\otimes_kH)$. Let $j_1(h)=h\otimes1$ and $j_2(h)=1\otimes h$. Componentwise tensor multiplication gives $j_1*j_2=\Delta_H$. For any algebra map $u:H\to H\otimes_kH$, the two antipode axioms give $u*(uS_H)=(uS_H)*u=\eta\epsilon_H$. Thus $\Delta_HS_H$ is an inverse of $\Delta_H$, and $j_iS_H$ is an inverse of $j_i$. Associativity shows $(j_2S_H)*(j_1S_H)$ is also an inverse of $j_1*j_2$. Inverses are unique: if $p*a=1=a*q$, then $p=p*(a*q)=(p*a)*q=q$. Applying this identity and evaluating at $h$ gives
$$\Delta_H(S_H(h))=\sum S_H(h_{(2)})\otimes S_H(h_{(1)}).$$
Only the cited convolution multiplication, unit and associativity and the given Hopf axioms enter this short calculation; no cocommutativity or bijectivity of $S_H$ is assumed.

proof.text:
Finally evaluate the claimed diagonal compatibility on its final $H^*$ factor at $x$. Its right side evaluates, by step 2 with argument $S_H(h_{(2)})x$, multiplicativity of $\Delta_H$, and step 5, to
$$\begin{aligned}
\sum h_{(1)}f_{(-1)}f_{(0)}(S_H(h_{(2)})x)
&=\sum h_{(1)}T_f(S_H(h_{(2)})x)\\
&=\sum h_{(1)}S_H(h_{(2)})x_{(2)} f(S_H(h_{(3)})x_{(1)}).
\end{aligned}$$
Apply the antipode axiom to the first two factors of $(\Delta_H\otimes1)\Delta_H(h)$ and then the counit identity. This gives $\sum h_{(1)}S_H(h_{(2)})\otimes h_{(3)}=1\otimes h$; applying $1\otimes S_H$ gives $\sum h_{(1)}S_H(h_{(2)})\otimes S_H(h_{(3)})=1\otimes S_H(h)$. Consequently the last displayed expression is
$$\sum x_{(2)}f(S_H(h)x_{(1)})=T_{h\cdot f}(x),$$
which is the evaluation of $\rho(h\cdot f)$. Reconstruction from step 2 proves the tensor equality. Together with steps 1, 3 and 4 this proves every clause.
